account: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) posted its Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million pilot from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the number of totally damaged houses predicted by the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model. The framework says that the model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. 510's 2024 paper in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences (vendor-authored) states that the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's June 2025 report says that the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached, and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million from CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. Under it, OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. The framework also adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports that nearly US$6 million was released and that WFP alone reached 42,100 families. An after-action review was held in April 2026. OCHA's framework for 2026 and 2027, endorsed on 22 October 2026, keeps the 510 model as the activation trigger for Regions 2, 3, 5 and 8. It states that the 2025 activation came from the observational trigger. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.

ai_role.statement: OCHA's 2021, 2023 and 2025 frameworks name the IFRC/510 impact model as the activation-trigger model. The 2021 framework describes it as partially a machine learning model. This is documented by the deployer, not only the maker. The model's forecasts were monitored during the December 2021 near activation (Typhoon Rai) without meeting criteria. The 2024 readiness phase for Pepito ended with CERF AA resources reallocated to response. OCHA's flash update attributes the 6 November 2025 activation for Uwan to the observational threshold (forecast peak 195 km/h against the 185 km/h trigger). It does not state that the 510 model's estimates reached the activation matrix. The AI's contribution to any payout is therefore not established. The maker's NHESS paper is the only source describing the algorithm (XGBoost).

fields.account: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) posted its Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021. It set up a US$7.5 million pilot from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the number of totally damaged houses predicted by the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model. The framework says that the model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. 510's 2024 paper in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences (vendor-authored) states that the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's June 2025 report says that the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached, and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million from CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. Under it, OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. The framework also adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports that nearly US$6 million was released and that WFP alone reached 42,100 families. An after-action review was held in April 2026. OCHA's framework for 2026 and 2027, endorsed on 22 October 2026, keeps the 510 model as the activation trigger for Regions 2, 3, 5 and 8. It states that the 2025 activation came from the observational trigger. No cited document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.
